items.note: In the newsletter strip, the email field now has a red border. Under it is a red circle icon and the line 'Enter a valid email address, like name@example.com', so the person knows what went wrong and how to fix it. Subscribe stays an ink lift button, so the pink hero CTA is the only pink action on the page.

On the dark raised strip, the field has a red border and the error line with its icon reads clearly. Subscribe is the paper-filled inverse button, shown lifted with its hard offset shadow, as the dark mapping asks. Nothing overlaps.
At phone width the field and the ink Subscribe button sit on one row. The red border and the icon-led message wrap cleanly onto two lines under the field, and nothing is clipped.

The form is replaced by a raised card with an ink border, a pink check dot and 'Thanks for subscribing. New posts will arrive at reader@example.com.' It is clearly a confirmation in the system's outlined-card language.
The same confirmation card shows on the dark strip, with a light border, a pink check and readable paper text. It is easy to tell the signup worked.
On mobile the confirmation card fills the column. The pink check sits beside the two-line thanks message, and spacing above and below matches the rest of the page.

The search field shows the pink halo focus ring with a clear ×, and the count reads 'Showing 0 of 6 posts'. Below is the empty state: a 'No posts match these filters' title, a yellow-and-pink magnifier sticker, one sentence ('Try a different tag or a shorter search.') and one pink 'Clear filters' lift button. The band strip inside the card was already raised as a minor in review 1.

Same layout on black: the halo ring on the field and the pink 'Clear filters' button are both readable. The magnifier sticker's outline turns paper-white in dark, the same thing review 1 already raised for the coin sticker, so it is not raised again.

The focused field with its × fills the column, and the pill strip scrolls off to the right. The empty card stacks the title strip, the magnifier, one sentence and the pink 'Clear filters' button. The hero's pink CTA is far above it, so only one pink action is on screen.
Focus is on the ink 'Home' pill in the top bar. A 2px ring at a 2px offset follows the pill's full radius, so it is clearly visible and nothing is clipped.
In dark, the paper-filled current 'Home' pill has a pink focus ring at an offset that follows its radius. The ring stands out against the dark header bar.
On mobile the focused 'Home' pill shows the same offset ring around the ink fill. The ring is fully inside the header, with nothing cut off at the top or bottom.

The hero has five tilted shapes on yellow, cropped by the edges: a pink coin with a plus and a yellow rim, a pink star, a pink arrow, a speech tag and a yellow coin with a pink rim. Each has a heavy ink outline and an extruded rim, built to the coin recipe. The featured card's pink bookmark on a yellow tile reads clearly at card size.

The article figure is a sticker scene on a yellow frame: three tilted pink and yellow bars (grouped variants) next to a coin with a check and an ink rim. It shows the caption's 'forty-one buttons, six actual jobs' idea, with ink outlines and token fills.

The figure has a dense yellow page, a pink arrow and a pink page with fewer, bolder lines. It reads at once as the same release rewritten for its readers. Heavy ink outlines and flat token fills only.

Three small square tiles on a blue band each hold one distinct ink-outlined sticker: a pink pencil, a box with an up arrow and an open pink book. Each is a different object built from basic shapes, and each reads at its small size.

The only motion captured is the hero sticker's scroll-bound 'drift': linear, iteration 1. Because the page is not scrolled, all eight frames from 36 to 654ms stay still. That matches the spec: the motion is scroll-bound and nothing loops on its own.
